cards.text: Jacob's brother Esau is coming to meet him with four hundred men (Genesis 32:6). In great fear and distress, Jacob sends herds of gifts on ahead (Genesis 32:7, 13-21). During the night he takes his two wives, his two maidservants and his eleven sons across the ford of the Jabbok and sends them over the stream with everything he owns.

cards.question: With his family across the Jabbok, Jacob keeps a few servants with him for the night.

cards.text: So Jacob is left all alone, and there a man wrestles with him until daybreak. I spent YEARS in the dark in a junk drawer, friend, and the roughest thing that ever jumped me was a rubber band.

cards.question: As they wrestle until daybreak, the man finds that he can overpower Jacob.
When the man sees he can't overpower Jacob, what does he do?

answers.text: He strikes the socket of Jacob's hip
He calls out for Jacob's servants
He lets go and slips off into the dark

cards.text: Jacob's hip is dislocated, and the man says, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.” Friend, I let go of a cookie sheet if it's a LITTLE warm, but Jacob says he won't let go unless the man blesses him.

The man asks Jacob his name, then says his name will no longer be Jacob. Most folks need a stack of forms and a LONG line to change their name, friend, and Jacob gets his changed while he's still hanging on.

cards.question: What new name does the man give Jacob?
The man says Jacob gets the name Israel because he has struggled with God and with men, and he has ___.

cards.text: Now Jacob asks, “Please tell me your name.” Fair enough, friend, because if you wrestle somebody till DAYBREAK, you want to know who it is.

cards.question: Instead of giving his name, the man replies, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he ___ Jacob there.
Jacob names the place Peniel. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He has seen God face to face and his life was spared
He has won the hardest fight of his whole life
He has finally made peace with his brother Esau

cards.text: The sun rises above Jacob as he passes by Penuel. Long night, friend. LONG night.

cards.question: As the sun rises over him, Jacob is limping because of his hip.
When this was written, the Israelites still didn't eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip. Why not?

answers.text: Jacob's hip was struck near that tendon
That tendon was set aside for the priests
That tendon was used to make bowstrings

cards.text: Hang on to your apron, friend. Jacob's story keeps going, and I'm not saying another WORD about it yet.
